newsitem.title: HONG KONG: COSCO Pac to buy US$360 mln containers.
newsitem.headline: COSCO Pac to buy US$360 mln containers.

text.p: Container leasing and terminal operating firm COSCO Pacific Ltd said in a statement on Monday it will spend HK$2.79 billion (US$360 million) in 1997 to buy 90,000 TEU (20-foot equivalent units) containers.
That will increase its capacity by 26.2 percent, it said.
But the firm aimed at raising its capacity by 27.5 percent this year, chairman Chen Zhongbiao said in the statement.

"We have increased our container fleet by 17.9 percent (in 1996), and in 1997 we are committed to increasing capacity by a further 27.5 percent to keep pace with the growth of our parent which will take delivery of 13 new vessels in 1997 and 1998," he said.
Its ultimate parent, China Ocean Shipping (Group) Co (COSCO), is its largest single customer.
COSCO controls COSMO Pacific through wholly-owned subsidiary C0SCO (Hong Kong) Group Ltd.
The listed firm's container fleet rose 17.9 percent to 343,245 TEU in 1996.

"As China's economy continues to grow, so will the marine transportation operations of COSCO, which will result in greater demand for container leasing, container terminal operations and the container related industries on which COSCO Pacific is focused," Chen said.
